answer: The place where I relax most completely is actually the rooftop of our building, which offers a surprisingly lovely view over the town. We live on the third floor, so it is just a short climb up the stairs, and on a clear evening you can see the rooftops stretching out towards the river. I go up there most evenings, especially after a long or stressful day at the office. There is something wonderfully [[liberating]] about being up high, away from the noise and crowds below. I usually take a cup of tea, put on some quiet music and simply watch the sky change colour as the sun goes down. Some of our neighbours grow plants in pots up there, so it feels almost like a small garden. The gentle breeze is genuinely [[refreshing]], and it seems to clear my head. What makes it so relaxing is the sense of [[solitude]]; it is my own little escape where no one bothers me. I often do my best thinking there, or sometimes just switch off entirely. During the monsoon I stand under the shelter of the stairwell and watch the rain sweep across the town, which is strangely calming. My job involves a lot of talking and problem-solving, so I need a moment to [[unwind]] before dinner with my family. Honestly, having a spot like this has been [[invaluable]] for my mental wellbeing. It costs nothing, yet it does more for my mood than almost anything else.

followUps.q: Do you ever go up there with other people?
followUps.answer: Occasionally. My younger sister sometimes comes up after she finishes studying, and during Eid the whole family goes up in the evening. Mostly, though, I prefer to keep it as my own quiet time.

followUps.q: Is it easy to find places to relax in your town?
followUps.answer: Not always. Sirajganj is fairly calm compared with Dhaka, but it is still getting busier, and most public places are quite noisy. That is why a private spot like our rooftop is so valuable.

note: View of the city changed to the town (third-floor flat); added plants, monsoon rain, why work makes him need it; added mark 'unwind'.
